messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in New York with reading room and fiction section, in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and children section, and in Chicago with cafe and reading room. We need to use the function public_library_find_nearby. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby({location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]}) => any.

We need to call the function three times, each with appropriate location and facilities. The facilities parameter expects a single value or an array? The type says "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]". That seems ambiguous: maybe it's a union of string or array of strings? The example says "Cafe"[] meaning array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe" type? But "Cafe" is a string literal type. So array of "Cafe" means array of string "Cafe"? That seems odd. Probably they want an array of facilities. So we can pass an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc.

Thus we need to call the function three times. We'll produce calls.
